title: Private upgrade choreographer and canary migration play
creator: Ava Kim
description: Design and implement a stateful 'upgrade choreographer' for Redwood Private that runs coordinated, observable, and reversible upgrades across VPC/on-prem clusters. The choreographer manages multi-step upgrades (agent, control-plane, DB schema changes, runtime kernels) using a declarative plan, embedded preflight checks, and a canary-first rollout strategy. This ticket covers the MVP operator, the canary migration policy, and integration points with Private's upgrade channels (LTS and rolling channels).
background: Current private upgrade workflows are ad-hoc: CLI-driven, manual sequencing, and require operator intervention for schema changes. We need a repeatable, auditable automation layer that reduces human error for customers and enables safe LTS rollouts. Goals: minimize downtime, provide deterministic rollback, enable controlled canaries, and emit rich telemetry for the Console. This complements recent investments in Private packaging and the on-prem upgrade sequencer prototypes.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can accept a declarative upgrade plan and execute it across a target Private cluster with observable phases
Canary policy: ability to run upgrades on a configurable subset of nodes (by tag/region) and automatically gate broader rollout based on health signals
Safe DB migrations: online migrator integration with explicit preflight dry-run and cutover window; automatic fallback if critical errors detected
Rollback: operator can perform automated rollback for last step or full plan; rollback path validated in tests
Console integration: upgrades appear in Console audit log with per-step status, tokenized timing, and cost estimate after run
Security: upgrade artifacts (images/manifests) validated against allowlist and signed with customer KMS where configured
implementation_notes: Operator shape: Kubernetes controller-style state machine for Private control plane; for on-prem without k8s, provide a light supervisor that executes same state machine over SSH/agent RPC
Upgrade plan format: YAML spec with ordered phases, each phase has preflight checks, exec steps, canary selectors, timeout, and rollback strategy
Canary gating signals: heartbeats, API latency p50/p95, pod OOMs, error rate, node-level kernel panic / GPU health; map signals to boolean gates
Schema migration strategy: two-phase safe migration (backward compatible write and read paths) + online migrator that performs nonblocking transforms + final prune step during low traffic window
KV cache and model artifacts: introduce artifact version pinning and atomic swap to avoid cache incoherence during rollout
Telemetry: emit per-plan and per-phase metrics via existing telemetry pipeline (Console ingestion), annotate traces with plan_id and step_id
Testing: end-to-end harness: minikube/kind-based integration tests + onprem simulated cluster using vm-based nodes to validate rollback, timeouts, and failure injection
APIs: expose REST endpoints for plan submit, status, abort, and dry-run. Integrate with CLI and Console for guided rollouts
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Ticket created after spike with Platform Release team. Decided to call the controller 'choreographer' to emphasize sequencing semantics.
2026-03-04: Architecture review with Infra and Security. Agreed on two runtime implementations (k8s-controller and agent-supervisor) to cover both VPC and air-gapped customers.
2026-03-06: Prototype of plan YAML drafted: includes phases, canary.selector, preflight.checks, and rollback.strategy. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1UpgradeChoreographerDraft

2026-03-08: Trade-off discussion: synchronous vs. asynchronous DB migrations. Chose online migrator (asynchronous, idempotent) to reduce host-level downtime; preflight dry-run required for non-idempotent steps.
2026-03-10: Implemented initial state machine scaffolding (internal branch). Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/67
2026-03-12: Canary gate metrics set finalized: p95 latency, API error-rate (>0.5% fails gate), db migration roll-forward errors. Next: add failure injection tests and Console UI hooks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: DB migration mistakes could cause data loss. Mitigation: require opt-in two-phase migrations + mandatory backup snapshot and automatic abort on migration assert failures.
Risk: Canary signals noisy on small clusters. Mitigation: allow synthetic traffic generation for canary validation and minimum sample size enforcement.
Risk: Customers with strict change windows. Mitigation: provide scheduling window and manual approval gate in operator.
Risk: Signing/allowlist mismatch in air-gapped installs. Mitigation: add offline artifact verification step and provide tool for local allowlist generation.
qa_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and rollback paths
Integration tests that simulate network partitions and node failures during each phase
Staging run against an internal VPC cluster with 10+ nodes, run multiple upgrade plans including DB prune step
Customer pilot with two existing Private customers (opt-in) to validate UI and rollback UX
